title: Trump Calls Modi 'a Very Tough Man' as Quad Leaders Meet in Manila
excerpt: At the first in-person Quad leaders' summit since 2024, Trump praised Modi and Takaichi's toughness while Modi pressed the four nations to set concrete goals on supply chains, technology and security.
body:
• US President Donald Trump called Prime Minister Narendra Modi "a very tough man" and "a great leader" as the four Quad leaders met in Manila on Tuesday, November 17, 2026 — the grouping's first in-person leaders' summit since September 2024.
  • Modi described the Quad as a "constructive and trusted partnership" and pressed the leaders to set concrete goals for its next phase, from maritime security to trusted supply chains.
  • The Manila meeting is expected to launch a Quad Business Leaders' Forum, with the four countries' export credit agencies meeting in Tokyo on November 18 to work out financing for joint projects, ANI reported.
  • Trump pointed to rare earths as an early test of that cooperation, saying the partners would have everything they need within 10 months.

US President Donald Trump heaped praise on Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Manila on Tuesday, calling him "a very tough man" and "a great leader" as the leaders of the Quad — the United States, India, Japan and Australia — held their first in-person summit since September 2024, on the sidelines of the 49th ASEAN Summit in the Philippine capital.

Speaking to reporters alongside Modi, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, Trump said, according to The Times of India: "He is a tough man. He is my friend. He is a great leader and respected all over the world." He added that Washington and New Delhi had "outstanding relationships" and were coordinating closely.

"And by the way, he's a very tough man, just in case. And she may be even tougher. And we're okay, too."

— Donald Trump, on PM Modi and Japanese PM Sanae Takaichi

Trump described his fellow leaders as "phenomenal people" and friends, ANI reported. "We have a great relationship with these people and these countries, and we have right from the beginning," he said. "I've been with all three of them for a long time, and they're phenomenal people, and they're friends of mine, so that helps. That really helps." The meeting was the first Quad leaders' summit of Trump's current term; the previous in-person summit was hosted by then-President Joe Biden in Wilmington, Delaware, on September 21, 2024.

Modi presses for concrete goals

Modi used his opening remarks to push the grouping from statements toward deliverables. "For India, the Quad is a constructive and trusted partnership. From maritime security to trusted supply chains, new technologies to disaster response, it has been our endeavour that the Quad provides trusted solutions," he said, according to The Times of India. He said he was confident the meeting would help set concrete goals for the next phase of cooperation, and noted that Manila has a special connection with the grouping: officials from the four countries first met in the city in 2007, and the Quad dialogue was revived there a decade later, in 2017. Modi also noted that the four foreign ministers have met five times since January last year, evidence, he said, of the partners' political will and shared commitment.

From strategic talk to commercial action

The clearest expected outcome from Manila is economic. ANI reported that the four nations are expected to set up an inaugural Business Leaders' Forum, bringing together industry leaders, policymakers and government officials to unlock investment in advanced manufacturing, clean energy and digital infrastructure, with semiconductors and critical minerals at the centre. Representatives of the four countries' export credit agencies will meet in Tokyo on November 18 to work out practical financing mechanisms for joint projects across the region. Another expected outcome is a Super Intelligence Accelerator, aimed at advancing cooperation in artificial intelligence and advanced computing across the Indo-Pacific. The initiatives follow the Quad foreign ministers' meeting in October, where the four countries announced plans to strengthen private-sector engagement and cooperation on economic security.

Trump highlighted supply chains directly. "We're doing very well. We are making rare earth at a level that we've never made before. We're gonna catch them within 10 months," he said, referring to dominant global suppliers. "Everything that we need, we'll have in 10 months. We're producing major numbers when it comes to rare earth, and they are too, by the way. Japan is, India is, we are all doing it."

What happens next

The Manila stop is the first on Trump's three-day Asia tour. From the Philippines he travels to China for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meetings and bilateral talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, IANS reported; asked about a separate sit-down with Russian President Vladimir Putin, Trump said, "I don't know, but I would. If it's available, I would do that." For the Quad itself, the test of the Manila meeting will be whether the Business Leaders' Forum and the Tokyo financing talks produce funded projects — the concrete goals Modi asked for.
